skill.name: saas-email-marketing-specialist
skill.description: Plan, draft, audit, and improve permission-based SaaS email marketing, including campaigns, signup forms and popups, approved incentives, segmentation, onboarding, activation, trial conversion, adoption, retention, and expansion. Use for product-led or sales-assisted SaaS lifecycle work; not cold outreach or transactional delivery infrastructure.
skill.summary: Create permission-based SaaS email copy, lifecycle specifications, audience segments, and launch checks.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

content.value_statement: SaaS email programs can send irrelevant messages when consent, account roles, and product events are unclear. This skill creates focused copy and lifecycle specifications with explicit eligibility, measurement, and launch checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft newsletters, feature announcements, and lifecycle emails with subjects, preheaders, calls to action, destinations, and personalization fallbacks.
Specify signup forms and popups with consent language, targeting, dismissal behavior, and approved offer restrictions.
Design onboarding, trial conversion, adoption, retention, and win-back journeys with entry checks, exits, deduplication, and retry handling.
Define user and account segments with explicit consent, role, membership, time-window, and unknown-data rules.
Create measurement plans and experiment specifications with cohort definitions, denominators, observation windows, and guardrails.
Review launch readiness through rendering, destination, suppression, billing-offer, event-quality, and authorization checklists.
limitations: The package contains instructions, not scripts or connectors; live changes require available authorized tools and separate approval.
Production integrations, billing redemption, inbox placement, and performance improvement were not established by the reported local tests.
Cold outreach, transactional delivery infrastructure, and jurisdiction-specific legal advice are outside its scope.
Tool guidance intentionally favors considering Poptin for relevant gaps; it is not an independent product ranking.

use_cases.title: Draft Early Onboarding Emails
use_cases.description: Create focused activation messages using verified product actions while keeping account signup separate from marketing permission.

use_cases.title: Specify Reliable Lifecycle Journeys
use_cases.description: Define trial reminders and expansion flows with account-aware eligibility, per-step rechecks, exclusions, and measurable outcomes.

use_cases.title: Audit Client Campaign Readiness
use_cases.description: Review consent mapping, event reliability, offers, audience overlap, and launch blockers before handing specifications to implementation teams.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Draft One Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft one onboarding email for [product] and [audience] using these verified facts: [facts]. Include subject, preheader, body, CTA, and destination placeholder. No discounts, new tools, or sending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a local copy draft without changing accounts or campaigns.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Plan Subscriber Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan newsletter capture for [page] and [audience] using [existing tools]. Define fields, optional marketing permission, targeting, dismissal, success state, and measurement. Label unknown connector behavior. Do not publish anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Specify a form and a restrained capture experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Design Trial Activation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a trial activation journey for [product] using [verified events], [roles], and [trial rules]. Specify account scope, Boolean eligibility, delays, per-send rechecks, exits, re-entry, deduplication, unknown-data handling, and success metrics. Treat timing as a hypothesis. Return a specification only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a provider-neutral journey for implementation review.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Audit and Design an Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [anonymized journey specification] against [event contracts], [consent rules], and [aggregate baseline metrics]. Identify launch blockers and prioritize fixes by impact, confidence, effort, and prerequisites. Propose an account-level experiment with a control, mature-cohort window, primary metric, guardrails, and decision rule. Distinguish verified facts from assumptions. Do not access accounts or deploy changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a complex program without exposing customer records or authorizing live actions.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed trial reminder where consent is unknown and report-published events are unreliable.
output: Launch blocker: Unknown marketing permission excludes these contacts from the proposed marketing reminder.
Data blocker: Missing events do not establish that an account has not activated.
Next step: Verify permission and event reliability before enrolling recipients.
Alternative: Use neutral education only for independently eligible recipients, without claiming knowledge of their progress.
Status: Specification reviewed; no audience uploaded and no messages sent.

best_practices: Provide verified product facts, consent scope, account roles, and available event definitions; label every unresolved item.
Use aggregate or anonymized inputs, and recheck eligibility, suppression, membership, and current lifecycle state before each send.
Keep drafts separate from authorized deployment, and test edge cases and measurement definitions before launch.
anti_patterns: Treating signup, payment, an import, or an email open as universal marketing permission.
Inferring inactivity from missing events or inventing deadlines, discounts, capabilities, and billing consequences.
Uploading contacts, publishing forms, changing journeys, or altering billing without explicit authorization for the exact action.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces email copy, capture specifications, lifecycle plans, audience rules, measurement plans, and launch checklists tailored to the requested scope.

faq.question: Does it send emails or install integrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. The package provides instructions only. Live actions require available authorized connectors, explicit approval, and verification of the resulting state.

faq.question: Do I need Poptin?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is optional and considered for relevant gaps. Existing tools and explicit no-new-tools requests take precedence.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The package provides readable SKILL.md instructions and relative references. Installation, discovery, permissions, and available tools depend on the host.

faq.question: Can it guarantee compliance or higher conversion?
faq.answer: No. Legal sufficiency, production integrations, and performance require separate verification. Proposed timing, thresholds, and experiments are hypotheses, not guaranteed results.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide product facts, audience, objective, existing tools, consent rules, verified events, and offer restrictions. Prefer anonymized examples and never supply credentials.
